contributions.statement: When building an LLM judge for content quality, use a direct rubric prompt with a few examples and spend the effort on a small human-labelled calibration set per criterion rather than checklist decomposition; decomposition gave no consistent gain and HD-Eval's reported gains came from its human-label-trained aggregator.
contributions.evidence: §6.1 Table 1 (Claude-4): TopicalChat rho direct 0.70-0.72 vs HD-Eval 0.56-0.58; SummEval the authors' own decomposition wins slightly. Appendix C Table 3: L1-agnostic HD-Eval (25 generic criteria + human-label regressor) matches standard HD-Eval. Single run, no significance tests; NLG summarization/dialogue, not code.
relative_to: validate LLM judges against human labels (P18)

reason: A clean negative result with an ablation that locates the gain in human labels, not pipeline complexity; useful if the team grades educational content with an LLM judge, irrelevant to code.
